name: Tools for Schools
headline: Read the behaviour. Pick the right tool.
intro: Training that helps school staff read what sits behind a behaviour and respond without escalating it.
glance: 6 hours in person, or 2 hours live online

problem.scene: Period 1. A pupil throws his book and walks out.
problem.question: By break he has a detention. Nobody has asked him why.
without: The same sanction as everyone else
with: Staff read what sits behind it
Staff know who to call and when
problem.standards: The DfE's Behaviour in Schools guidance (2024) expects staff to consider underlying factors and put support in place alongside sanctions. This course shows staff how to do it in the moment.
problem.evidence: It works alongside your behaviour policy, not instead of it. Ideally the whole staff team trains together, so everyone shares a language.

groups: For children in care and previously in care
The people who set and review the behaviour policy
notes: Best with the whole staff team

outcomes: See the school day from their side
Describe a school day from the side of a child in care, including what adults often miss.
Recognise how attachment difficulties and trauma show up in a classroom, a corridor and a detention.
Tell when a child can think
Use the window of tolerance to tell when a child can think and when they can't.
Explain how labels and low expectations shape how a child is treated, using Goffman and Rosenthal.
Use de-escalation phrases and hold the boundary while showing the child you understand why.
Rewrite a pupil profile without labels, and know when to contact the virtual school and social worker.

pillars.title: The tools your staff take back to school
pillars.stance: Read the behaviour, then reach for the right tool
pillars.stance_line: Practised in the room, with handouts to keep, and ready for the next morning.
items: A quick way to tell when a child is calm enough to think, and when they are not.
Fewer words, a calm voice, the boundary held in a tense moment.
A pupil profile that is accurate, says what helps, and doesn't label.
Hold the boundary while responding to the reason underneath.
pillars.base: Built on Siegel's window of tolerance, Bowlby's attachment theory, Louise Bombèr's work in schools, and Goffman on stigma.

story_line: Two stories run through the day: Tyler, 12, in his second secondary school this year, and Amira, 8, after half term. Each is a composite, drawn from real experiences of care.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.

He has worked with councils nationally on children in care in schools, including Middlesbrough's town-wide programme to make every school attachment aware and trauma informed, and Darlington, where designated teachers designed their own training with him.
Teachers are one of the largest groups he trains, and he has spoken at national and regional virtual school conferences.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
